name: BrowserAct

modes.label: Cloud Bot managed browser
modes.note: There is NO time-based meter. Cloud browser runtime and the built-in dynamic proxy are 'free for a limited time' (no end date, no post-promo rate). Cost is per action: Workflow Bot 3 credits per executed step (pricing page; the docs still say 5), Agent Bot build 300-1,500 credits plus 10-30 credits per run (estimates). Credit value: list $0.0020; Basic $0.0016 (monthly) / $0.0013 (annual); Essential $0.0014 / $0.00112; Advanced $0.0012 / $0.00096. 'As low as' $0.00064 is not tied to any published plan. So one workflow step costs $0.0029-$0.0048, and a browser-hour costs steps_per_hour x 3 x $/credit: 60 steps/h = $0.17-$0.29/h; 720 steps/h (one per 5 s) = $2.07-$3.46/h. Monthly capacity is 3,333 / 16,667 / 33,333 steps on Basic / Essential / Advanced.

network.residential_proxy_gib_note: 5,000 credits/GB is $10 at list, $8 (Basic monthly), $6.50 (Basic annual), $7 / $5.60 (Essential), $6 / $4.80 (Advanced monthly / annual), and 'as low as $3.2/GB'. The built-in dynamic proxy for Cloud Bots is currently free (promo), so the per-GB charge applies to Local CLI / Agent CLI use. BYO proxy is free. Static proxy is credits per proxy per month by location and tier, not public.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: Free: $0, 200 signup credits (one-time, first account per IP), 2 free Agent builds, 2 simultaneous tasks, 5 free local browsers. Credit Packs are not available on Free. Paid plans: 7-day free trial for new users with 1,000 / 1,500 / 2,000 trial credits (Basic / Essential / Advanced).

plans.name: Basic monthly displayed promo
plans.note: 10 k monthly credits; crossed-out 20 list; up to 5 static proxies, 10 local browsers.

plans.name: Essential monthly displayed promo
plans.note: 50 k credits; crossed-out 100; up to 25 static proxies, 50 local browsers.

plans.name: Advanced monthly displayed promo
plans.note: 100 k credits; crossed-out 200; up to 50 static proxies, 100 local browsers.

features.ip_note: Hosted rotating residential Dynamic Proxy at 5,000 credits/GB (~$8/GB on Basic $16/10k credits; 'as low as $3.2/GB' at best rate); static dedicated proxies priced monthly by location; custom HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy supported.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
All paid monthly displayed prices are discounted versus crossed-out values: label as promotional, not unconditional permanent list price. Annual switch captured in Chrome.
Local browser fees do not buy a hosted computer. Cloud runtime and built-in dynamic proxy are free for a limited time only, while task credits remain billable.
Agent build/run figures are estimates and percentages, not exact fixed step tariffs. Static proxy price varies by location and tier, not disclosed.

No overage and no pay-as-you-go: when credits hit zero, tasks pause ('The current automation step will finish before execution pauses. Proxy connections pause when the Credit balance reaches zero.'). The only top-up is Credit Packs, which are for subscribers only (not the Free plan), expire at the next monthly reset, are non-refundable, and have no public price.

CONFLICT between official pages on the Workflow step price: pricing page and www llms.txt say 3 credits per executed step ('starting from approximately $0.0019 per step'); docs billing-credits says '1 executed step = 5 credits' (Loop = loop count x 5, Loop List = item count x 5, Scroll to element = scroll count x 5). The pricing page is treated as current; the docs value is 67% higher.

Monthly credits never roll over (they reset on the monthly anniversary at 00:00 UTC, also on annual plans). Subscriptions and credit packs are non-refundable. Annual = 20% off, with credits still allotted monthly. Monthly-to-annual switching requires cancelling and re-buying from the next cycle. An immediate upgrade charges the price difference and adds the credit difference (only if >48 h remain in the cycle).
No team seats: accounts are single-user ('do not include teammate invitations, member roles, or shared workspaces').

fleet.tiers: Free 2; Basic 10; Essential 20; Advanced 40 concurrent tasks; custom concurrency by contact.
fleet.notes: Cloud-task concurrency, not local-browser profile counts. 50/300/1,000 require custom arrangements; trial/payment checks and turnaround unspecified.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Cookies, cache, and browsing history are stored between runs.
snapshot_auto.note: Strict reading: 'Standard Browser' mode keeps a fixed Browser ID and persists the browser profile (cookies, cache, history) between Bot runs; this is profile persistence (persistent-disk analogue), not a saved machine/process state. No memory or open-tab state is restored. 'Private Browser' mode discards everything after the task.

harness_api.quote: Starts a new task execution for a published Bot and returns a `task_id`.
harness_api.note: REST API runs a pre-built published Bot (Workflow Built or Agent Built) with an input object matching its input_schema, plus status/resume/cancel and webhooks. No API to start an agent harness with a free-form prompt, stream its events or send follow-ups. Bots can also be exposed as MCP tools to external agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI), which is the reverse direction.

guest_firewall.quote: Entirely in the cloud. No setup is needed.
guest_firewall.note: Users configure Bots/workflows only; no shell or root access to the cloud browser host is offered, so no way to run nftables/iptables.

secret_proxy.quote: Credentials are encrypted and are not exposed to the platform, third parties, or language models without your authorization.
secret_proxy.note: Credential Center is an encrypted login vault with Website Auto-Login (username/password + TOTP) for Workflow Built Bots only; the platform fills website login forms in the cloud browser. Hidden from the LLM, but it is form-fill auto-login, not a proxy that injects credentials into outbound HTTP requests; no arbitrary-API or non-HTTP coverage.

image_oci.quote: BrowserAct manages the cloud browser environment, Bot runs, Tasks, and structured results, so you do not need to install a local Agent or maintain browser infrastructure.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - BrowserAct only offers a managed cloud Chromium browser plus a local CLI browser controller, never a custom OCI/Docker image boot target.

docker_inside.quote: BrowserAct Cloud is a cloud-based AI web data extraction platform.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - there is no shell/root access to the managed cloud browser host to run Docker; Agent CLI runs on the user's own machine/browser, not a provisioned container.

nested_virt.quote: Entirely in the cloud. No setup is needed.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - users configure Bots/workflows only, with no exposed compute/VM access to enable /dev/kvm.

desktop.quote: Human Interaction Node: Pauses the workflow and hands browser control to a human, then resumes automation after manual actions are completed.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - BrowserAct exposes a live browser view/handoff for a running Bot task (screenshot/live browser info via API), not a general-purpose VNC/RDP graphical desktop of the whole machine.

ssh.quote: BrowserAct manages the cloud browser environment, Bot runs, Tasks, and structured results, so you do not need to install a local Agent or maintain browser infrastructure.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no shell/SSH access to the managed cloud browser host is documented anywhere.

snapshot.quote: Cookies, cache, and browsing history are stored between runs.
snapshot.note: Standard Browser mode persists the browser profile (cookies/cache/history) between runs, but this is browser-profile persistence, not a disk or memory/process snapshot of a machine. No API/CLI to snapshot a whole machine state was found.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Starts a new task execution for a published Bot and returns a `task_id`.
snapshot_on_demand.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - the API surface covers Bots/tasks/proxy regions only; no snapshot/checkpoint endpoint exists.

fork.quote: Cross-browser parallelism ... Each browser has independent cookies, fingerprints, and proxy settings.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - new browsers/sessions are created fresh (or reuse a persistent profile); there is no clone/fork-a-running-machine capability documented.

fork_running.quote: A session belongs to the agent or task that created it. A session is tied to one browser.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no live clone-without-stopping capability documented.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: This model lets agents run multiple tasks without mixing state.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - fork itself is not offered, so memory-preserving fork is not offered.

pause_resume.quote: Requests the resumption of a paused Bot task.
pause_resume.note: Task-level pause/resume is a first-class API concept (Human Interaction Node also pauses a task for manual takeover, then resumes). This is at the task/Bot-run level, not a generic VM pause with reduced billing, but it is the provider's own pause/resume mechanism.

wake_on_request.quote: BrowserAct manages the cloud browser environment, Bot runs, Tasks, and structured results.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - there is no persistent addressable machine that sleeps and wakes on request; each task spins up a browser instance on demand instead.

persistent_disk.quote: Cookies, cache, and browsing history are stored between runs.
persistent_disk.note: Standard Browser mode keeps profile state (cookies/cache/history) across Bot runs, which is the closest analogue to persistent disk for this product; Private Browser discards everything.

volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - file handling is task-scoped output/download, not an attachable extra persistent volume.

volume_shared.quote: Multiple sessions on one browser ... Both sessions share the browser's cookies and profile, but navigation and current page state are separate.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no shared-volume-across-machines concept; only browser profile sharing across sessions of the same browser identity.

auto_stop_idle.note: Doc text (truncated in fetch) indicates idle sessions are reclaimed/closed automatically; cloud browser instances are also inherently ephemeral per-task rather than always-on, consistent with auto-stop-on-idle behavior.

live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - there is no user-controlled CPU/RAM sizing of the managed browser instance at all, let alone a live resize of a running one.

agent_harnesses.quote: Browser-act is an Agent CLI for browser automation.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - Browser-act is a browser-automation CLI/skill that a coding agent calls as a tool; BrowserAct does not ship or preinstall general coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) inside a sandbox.

own_agent_api.quote: Starts a new task execution for a published Bot and returns a `task_id`.
own_agent_api.note: First-party REST API drives BrowserAct's own browser/data-extraction agent (Agent Built / Workflow Built Bots): create task, poll/retrieve status, resume, cancel. This is the provider's own task/browser agent API, not a coding-harness API.

lang_python.quote: Install the CLI with `uv` and Python 3.12: uv tool install browser-act-cli --python 3.12
lang_python.note: The Agent CLI is a Python package (Python 3.12+ required) and the Cloud product exposes a REST API usable from any language including Python.

lang_node.quote: Python 3.12+ | Required by the CLI package
lang_node.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - the Agent CLI explicitly requires Python 3.12+ with no Node.js runtime/SDK documented; integrations (Zapier/Make/n8n/MCP) are via REST API/webhooks rather than a first-party Node SDK.

public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - the managed browser's outbound IP is a rotated residential proxy IP, not a dedicated public IPv4 assigned to a customer machine; no inbound public IPv4 concept exists for a managed browser product.

inbound_https.quote: BrowserAct manages the cloud browser environment, Bot runs, Tasks, and structured results.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - there are no user-exposed network ports on the managed browser; access is only via the BrowserAct API/UI, not an HTTPS URL to a port on the machine.

ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - access control is via account-level API keys, not per-machine ingress/IP allowlist rules, because there are no exposed inbound ports.

egress_allowlist.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no provider-side outbound allow/deny list or no-internet mode is documented; browsers can navigate to any target site by design.

egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no method/path level egress rules are documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: up to 5 static proxies, 10 local browsers
static_egress_ip.note: Paid plans include a quota of 'static proxies' (dedicated/static outbound proxy IPs), separate from the default rotating residential dynamic proxy; card also notes 'Static dedicated proxies priced monthly by location.'

gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - BrowserAct provides managed Chromium browsers for web data extraction, not general-purpose GPU compute.

windows.quote: Chrome or Chromium | Required for `chrome` and `chrome-direct` browser types
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - the product provisions cloud Chromium browser instances only; no Windows desktop/VM machine type is offered.

macos.quote: Chrome or Chromium | Required for `chrome` and `chrome-direct` browser types
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no macOS machine type is offered; the CLI itself runs cross-platform on the user's own machine but that is not a hosted macOS machine.

self_host.quote: BrowserAct manages the cloud browser environment, Bot runs, Tasks, and structured results, so you do not need to install a local Agent or maintain browser infrastructure.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - BrowserAct Cloud is a hosted SaaS; no self-hosted deployment package for the Cloud platform is offered (Agent CLI runs locally but is a client, not a self-hosted server).

byoc.quote: BrowserAct manages the cloud browser environment, Bot runs, Tasks, and structured results.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no bring-your-own-cloud-account deployment option is documented.

open_source.quote: Browser-act is an Agent CLI for browser automation.
open_source.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - the Cloud platform and CLI are distributed as a hosted product/PyPI package (browser-act-cli) with no OSI license documented; a GitHub skills repo exists but the core engine/product license is not published as open source.

arm64.quote: BrowserAct manages real cloud browsers, browser identities, proxies, and supported verification handling, reducing the infrastructure you need to maintain.
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. BrowserAct sells managed browser automation (Workflow/Agent Bots and a hosted Chromium browser) billed per credit/step, not selectable compute instances; there is no CPU-architecture choice exposed to customers anywhere in the pricing or docs.
